title: First-tier Tribunal HAV/43UJ/BSR/2025/0001: appeal against a Building Safety Regulator decision on escape from a roof-level bedroom over an open-plan ground floor
jurisdiction: England (UK): Secretary of State determination / appeal / tribunal under the Building Act 1984 and Building Regulations; comparative test only, not Alberta
code_edition: Building Regulations (edition for the BSR decision not confirmed in the excerpts); Building Act 1984 s.43A(3)

facts.text: The applicant appealed under section 43A(3) of the Building Act 1984 against a Building Safety Regulator decision; the regulator's decision is dated 14 March 2025.
The top storey is a bedroom built within the roof with dormer windows, and escape from this room is the subject of the appeal.
The ground floor is almost entirely open plan, with the staircase leading off the kitchen and living room.
The tribunal records no evidence as to why compartmentalisation of the staircase or other measures could not be provided, and describes the applicant's solution as cheap and impractical.

The regulator's witness is recorded as referring to a published case, APP/007/002/012 dated 18 April 2013, on relaxing a Part B requirement, and as being satisfied the issue was significantly different.
The hearing took place on 30 July 2025; the decision is dated 8 October 2025.
